title: The pipeline: two specialists in parallel, a merge, an evaluation, as one workflow on the queue
purpose: Run the design's workflow: two specialists train at the same time, a merge job waits for both, an evaluation job waits for the merge. Every step is a Job in the research queue; the workflow engine only orders them. Afterwards, trace the candidate back to its inputs from the records the runs wrote.

steps.display: kubectl apply -f combine-s10.yaml   # an Argo Workflow: four steps, each one a Kueue-managed Job
steps.output:
spec-math    after: -
spec-tools   after: -
merge        after: spec-math, spec-tools
evaluate     after: merge

checks.description: the workflow succeeded: all four steps ran to completion
checks.because: Each step creates one Indexed Job, waits for its success condition (a succeeded pod) or its failure condition, and reports to the controller.

checks.description: the two specialists ran at the same time (their step times overlap)
checks.because: The DAG gives the two specialists no dependency on each other, and the queue has four GPUs of quota, so both were admitted together.

checks.description: the merge started only after both specialists finished, and the evaluation only after the merge
checks.because: The dependencies are the workflow's only job: the merge reads the specialists' weights from the bucket, so it must not start before they are written.

checks.description: every step's job went through the research queue (a Kueue workload exists for each)
checks.because: The pipeline does not bypass admission: its jobs wait behind, and ahead of, other work by priority like any other.

checks.description: the candidate can be traced to its inputs: the evaluated model is the merge, the merge lists both specialists, each specialist records its family mix, step count and base model
checks.because: Every run writes its recipe as its first record, and the merge writes the runs it combined. Nothing was added by hand; the chain is read from the files.

checks.description: the pipeline ends in a gate decision that was computed, not assumed (the verdict is printed with the per-family changes)
checks.because: The last step compares the merged model with the untrained one per family with the same function the release gate uses.
